min_back_pressure_note: CRITICAL CORRECTION (Phase 6C): 'Min. back pressure' in Section 3.2 of the operating instructions is the MINIMUM back pressure of the TEST CONDITION ('ml' = max load test method) — it is NOT a maximum operating limit and NOT a thermal safety limit. At 60 Hz the minimum test back pressure was 50 Pa; at 50 Hz it was 0 Pa. Forward-curved fans are thermally at risk at LOW back pressure (free delivery), NOT high back pressure. This fan CANNOT be rejected on thermal-overload grounds based on this document alone. The aerodynamic performance curve (shutoff head, fan curve) is NOT contained in the operating instructions — a separate performance datasheet is required.

forward_curved_thermal_note: Forward-curved fans have an overloading power characteristic: motor power increases as flow increases (back pressure decreases). This means the thermal risk is at LOW back pressure (high flow / free delivery), not at high back pressure. The 'Min. back pressure' specification in the operating instructions is the lower bound of the safe test condition range, not an upper limit on system resistance. This fan is NOT disqualified on thermal grounds from the information in the operating instructions.
suitability_assessment: UNDER RE-EVALUATION. The Phase 6B rejection on thermal grounds (based on '50 Pa maximum back pressure') was incorrect — that value was a minimum test condition, not a maximum limit. The fan cannot be rejected on thermal grounds from the operating instructions alone. However, suitability for a filtration system (250-700 Pa system resistance) still depends on the aerodynamic fan curve (shutoff head) which is unknown. Forward-curved fans typically have lower shutoff heads than backward-curved fans of similar size; at 2.61 kg and 225mm equivalent size, the shutoff head may be inadequate. REMAINS TIER 3 pending performance datasheet.
recommended_action: Obtain the ebm-papst G2E140-AE77-01 PERFORMANCE DATASHEET (not the operating instructions). This is a different document containing the Q-ΔP fan curve. If the shutoff head is less than the expected system resistance (estimated 200-700 Pa), reject. If the shutoff head is in the useful range, re-evaluate for the appropriate scenario.
